root_cause.text: The driver assumed `dma_need_unmap()` would remain constant during PRP mapping, but it can change mid-iteration (e.g., due to swiotlb enabling), causing a NULL pointer dereference when accessing uninitialized `dma_vecs` while saving DMA mapping information for later unmapping.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The initial state of dma_needs_unmap may be false, but change to true while mapping the data iterator. Enabling swiotlb is one such case that can change the result. ... This fixes a NULL dereference from accessing an uninitialized dma_vecs when the device dma unmapping requirements change mid-iteration." The patch moves the allocation of `dma_vecs` from a one-time check at the start of `nvme_pci_setup_data_prp` into a per-segment function `nvme_pci_prp_save_mapping` that allocates on demand.

Author: Keith Busch <kbusch@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Sep 15 13:05:38 2017 -0400

    nvme-pci: Print invalid SGL only once
    
    The WARN_ONCE macro returns true if the condition is true, not if the
    warn was raised, so we're printing the scatter list every time it's
    invalid. This is excessive and makes debugging harder, so this patch
    prints it just once.
    
    Signed-off-by: Keith Busch <keith.busch@intel.com>
    Reviewed-by: Mart
